subject: science
intro: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion. Any moving object has kinetic energy. The amount of kinetic energy depends on the object's mass and its speed. More mass means more kinetic energy (at the same speed), and more speed means more kinetic energy (for the same mass). Speed has a bigger effect: doubling the speed increases kinetic energy by much more than doubling the mass, because kinetic energy depends on the speed squared. Graphs of data can show these relationships.

items.prompt: Two balls roll at the same speed, but one has twice the mass. Which has more kinetic energy?

steps: At the same speed, kinetic energy depends on mass.
The ball with more mass has more kinetic energy.
So the heavier ball has more kinetic energy.
solution.answer: The heavier ball, because more mass means more kinetic energy at the same speed.

items.prompt: A car speeds up from 10 km/h to 20 km/h. Does its kinetic energy just double? Explain.

steps: Kinetic energy depends on the speed squared, not just the speed.
Doubling the speed multiplies the kinetic energy by about four times.
So the kinetic energy more than doubles.
solution.answer: No; doubling the speed makes the kinetic energy about four times as large.

items.prompt: A graph shows kinetic energy rising steeply as speed increases. What does this tell you about how speed affects kinetic energy?

steps: A steep rise means small speed increases cause large energy increases.
This matches kinetic energy depending on speed squared.
So speed has a strong effect on kinetic energy.
solution.answer: Speed has a strong effect; kinetic energy rises steeply with speed.
